title: Traversable wormholes
example_questions: What if we went through a wormhole?
Could a wormhole connect two stars?
summary: General relativity allows wormholes, tunnels joining distant regions of space. Keeping one open long enough to travel through requires exotic matter that violates the null energy condition. Quantum effects can provide this in special theoretical setups (Gao, Jafferis and Wall), but those wormholes are no faster than going the long way round.
support_note: Mathematically allowed; no known way to build a macroscopic traversable wormhole.
what_happens: Two mouths connect through a short throat
Exotic matter holds the throat open
Light passing near a mouth is strongly lensed
objections: Needs exotic matter in large amounts
Could be turned into a time machine

sources.title: Wormholes in spacetime and their use for interstellar travel
sources.authors: M. S. Morris, K. S. Thorne

sources.title: Traversable wormholes via a double trace deformation
